text:
Dr. Jill Biden attends Jill Biden In Conversation With Whoopi Goldberg: View From The East Wing at 92NY on June 02, 2026 in New York City.

Following the release of her memoir, View from the East Wing, former first lady Dr. Jill Biden is telling all about her time in the White House.

In the book, she reflected on her husband’s decision to run for president in 2020. She revealed that the initial conversation was brief, lasting only about a minute during a lunch in December 2018 following George H.W. Bush's funeral.

"Before I even looked at the menu, I said: 'This is it, Joe. You have to make up your mind. Are you going to run or not?”

"'Yes, I want to run,' he told me matter-of-factly." To which she replied simply, “Ok.”

Already 78 when he entered office, he was the first president to turn 80 while in office, though he will soon be joined by President Donald Trump, who turns 80 later this month.

U.S. President Joe Biden and first lady Jill Biden cheer on members of the Wounded Warrior Project's Soldier Ride, on the South Lawn at the White House June 23, 2022 in Washington, DC. The event helps raise awareness to the public about severely injured veterans and provides rehabilitation opportunities.

As his term went on, Dr. Biden became increasingly aware of the toll the job and time itself were having on her husband.

She asked in the book, “Had he grown too old for the job and I hadn’t noticed?”

“I didn’t think so, could I be objective enough to be sure?"

This became more and more prevalent as the prospect of serving another term in 2024 crept closer.

While watching the June 2024 debate against Donald Trump from a nearby holding room, she felt a sense of impending disaster. Observing Joe Biden's performance, she was struck by a fear that he was suffering a medical emergency, even asking herself, "Is this a stroke?"

In her book, she describes wondering if he had been drugged. "It felt like we were watching an AI hologram of the man we knew, and the hologram was glitching. Has he been drugged?"

Dr. Biden explained that she did her best to maintain a neutral stance regarding his decision to drop out of the race. She even refused to provide an answer when he asked directly for her opinion, instead saying she’d support him either way.

First lady Jill Biden and Hunter Biden, son of U.S. President Joe Biden, leave the J. Caleb Boggs Federal Building on June 11, 2024 in Wilmington, Delaware.

She also speaks about her children in the book. She shared a bit about her perspective on the challenges her stepson, Hunter, faced. This included his June 2024 federal criminal trial, which led to a guilty verdict regarding tax and gun charges. The court proceedings brought to light intimate and sometimes graphic accounts of his difficult years, involving drug use in motels alongside sex workers and various associates.

She also noted that she and her husband, during his time as vice president and the years following, experienced a period of being "partly in denial" regarding Hunter’s addiction. These struggles surfaced in the wake of his brother Beau’s passing from cancer in 2015.
